title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 6 close: no praevisa congruentia; Miserebor cujus misertus fuero
pass_a_gloss: To this first benefit, therefore, that some reason of justice may appear in it, we ought not to require some foreseen congruity in the elect: but to that extent this is just, inasmuch as it befits the divine will and goodness to will so to act, according to that, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy; not however, I will have mercy on those in whom, that I may at the same time do this justly, I shall have foreseen certain congruent merits.
pass_b_english: So for this first benefit, if some reason of justice is to appear in it, we must not require a foreseen congruity in the elect. It is just insofar as it befits the divine will and goodness to will to act so — according to I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy — not I will have mercy on those in whom, that I may do this justly at once, I shall have foreseen certain congruent merits.
source_text: Ad hoc igitur primum beneficium, ut appareat in eo ratio quaedam justitiae, non debemus requirere praevisam aliquam congruentiam in electis: sed eatenus hoc justum est, quatenus convenit voluntati et bonitati Divinae sic agere velle, juxta illud, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero; non autem, Miserebor illorum in quibus, ut hoc juste simul faciam, merita quaedam congrua praevidero.
